chienNous.jaugesTitre: The dogs that would suit you best
chienNous.invitationDuo: And what does your partner think? Take the quiz again together to see which questions you disagree on.
chienNous.noteFin: This quiz is a game. It gives you an idea but it doesn't replace the advice of a breeder or a vet. Before you adopt, go and meet the dog and talk to people who know the breed.
chienNous.p_golden_d: The golden retriever is a very gentle dog that gets on with everyone. It loves to play and it learns fast, which is why you see it in so many families. On the other hand, it needs a long walk every day and it sheds a lot.
chienNous.p_golden_a: Plan at least an hour's walk a day. A golden doesn't like being alone all day, so it's better if one of you comes home at lunchtime.
chienNous.p_refuge_d: You don't have a particular breed in mind, and that's absolutely fine. Your dog is probably waiting for you in a shelter. You won't know everything about its past, but the volunteers know it well. They can tell you if it gets on with children or with cats.
chienNous.p_refuge_a: Go and see it several times before you decide, and take it for a walk. An adult dog that's already house-trained is often easier than a puppy.
chienNous.p_corgi_d: The corgi is a small herding dog with a lot of energy. It's very clever and it loves to play. It follows you everywhere in the house. It's also a dog that barks easily, for example when someone rings the bell.
chienNous.p_corgi_a: It needs a real walk every day and games to keep it busy, otherwise it gets up to mischief. It also sheds all year round, so you'll need to brush it often.
chienNous.p_bouledogue_d: The French bulldog is a perfect dog for apartment life. It doesn't need to run for hours and it would rather nap against you on the sofa. It's funny and a bit stubborn. It also snores very loudly!
chienNous.p_bouledogue_a: It copes badly with heat and with hard exercise. Choose a serious breeder who pays attention to how well their dogs breathe, because that's the breed's weak point.
chienNous.p_cavalier_d: The Cavalier King Charles spaniel is a very cuddly little dog. It's easy to live with and it adapts to you. It enjoys a walk in the sun as much as an evening in front of a series. What it wants most is to be with you.
chienNous.p_cavalier_a: It really struggles with long days alone. Also ask the breeder if the parents' hearts have been checked, because that's the most common health problem in this breed.
chienNous.p_aussie_d: The Australian shepherd is a dog for sporty couples. It has a huge amount of energy and it learns a trick in a few minutes. It's also very attached to its owners, to the point of following you into the bathroom.
chienNous.p_aussie_a: It needs two hours of activity a day. Walking isn't enough, it also needs games or a dog sport. A bored Australian shepherd can do a lot of damage in the house.
chienNous.p_teckel_d: The dachshund is a small dog with a lot of character. It's brave and very attached to its owners. It's also quite stubborn, so it only obeys when it feels like it. It's happy in a small apartment and it loves sleeping under the duvet.
chienNous.p_teckel_a: Take care of its back, which is fragile. Avoid stairs and jumps off the sofa. When it comes to training, you'll have to be more stubborn than it is!
chienNous.p_caniche_d: The poodle is one of the most intelligent dogs. It understands quickly and it loves learning new tricks. It's close to its owners without being clingy. On top of that, it hardly sheds.
chienNous.p_caniche_a: Its coat never stops growing, so you need to take it to the groomer every six to eight weeks. It comes in several sizes, from the toy poodle to the standard poodle.
chienNous.p_shiba_d: The Shiba Inu is an independent dog that's a bit like a cat. It's calm at home and it hardly ever barks. It copes with being alone better than most dogs. It loves you, but it's not the kind of dog that stays glued to you all day.
chienNous.p_shiba_a: Because it's independent, it doesn't always come back when you call it. It's better to keep it on a lead outdoors. It also sheds a lot twice a year.
chienNous.p_husky_d: The Siberian husky is a sled dog that needs to burn off energy for hours. It needs exercise every day and a fairly cool climate. It's playful and very talkative. It doesn't bark but it howls like a wolf. It can also escape as soon as a door is left open.
chienNous.p_husky_a: It's a dog for very sporty couples with a well-fenced garden. In an apartment or in a hot region, it will be unhappy.
chienNous.p_bernois_d: The Bernese mountain dog is a very big dog of around ninety pounds, calm and very gentle. It likes quiet walks and it gets on well with children. It doesn't need to run, but it needs room and a climate that isn't too hot.
chienNous.p_bernois_a: With this dog, everything costs more, starting with the food. You also need a big car to carry it. You should also know that it doesn't live as long as other dogs, often between seven and ten years.
chienNous.p_peluche_d: According to your answers, it's not the right time to get a dog yet. Either nobody is home during the day, or you often go away. It may also be that one of you wants a dog more than the other. A real dog would spend a lot of time waiting for you.
chienNous.p_peluche_a: That doesn't mean you'll never have one. You can look after a friend's dog for a weekend or walk the dogs at a shelter. You'll soon see if you still want one.
